title: Father's switch from accordion to trumpet, Kaiser and teacher Asibiyah
summary: His father began on accordion; Kaiser, who ran a place in the District, urged him to switch to a blowing instrument, gave him a trumpet, and a French teacher taught him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: My father. What did your father play? He played trumpet. Oh, he played trumpet. He had the national office. The national? National office. No, no. Y'all don't have no pictures of it around here? No. I don't believe they're taking any pictures of it in the mids, you know. I don't believe they're taking them. Can you tell us anything more about your father? Going back to your father for a little while, can you tell us, do you know where he learned to play the trumpet? Well, he did. He started around a place called Pretty Grouse. That was around at Oldenst, Corn Island and Liberty. And then they had a place around here called 25. Yeah, I remember that. During the 10th Kennedy, what he had showed us, because he had started off on accordion. That was his first leading instrument played, accordion. And one of the gentlemen, he called Kaiser, he told him, he said, man, you play so swell on that accordion. He said, why don't you switch to some blowing instrument? Kaiser the one who plays safe on the clarinet? No, not him. This is the white drum. Oh, yeah? Oh, yeah? Yeah.

Seems like I heard of a man by the name of Kaiser that had a place they called the pig ankle or something where they'd kick the ham and all that. That's right. That's right. Absolutely. Down there in the district, near the 25. That's correct. Run by Kaiser. That's correct.

And he had given me his first trumpet. He told him, he said, well, man, you get off that squeeze box. That's what they call it. They said, I'll be playing so much squeeze box. I don't know that trumpet. And he started taking lessons with the fellow. Asibiyah, they called him. What's his name? A French fellow called Asibiyah. Asibiyah. Asibiyah. Asibiyah. That's what he used for his teacher. So he started writing his trumpet. And after he started writing his trumpet, when he started leading the band, the trumpet. After that. Do you know any more about this French teacher, Asibiyah? No. No, I don't exactly know because I was so young when he was teaching me that. He started learning.
